column8: Mon 16 Nov: store only, input to Q92-034; re-read at source: the notice is due 120 days before the term ends (election act Art. 34), not 120 days ahead of the vote, and the 30-day rule is that act's Art. 35, not Additional Articles Art. 2; the 20 Jan 2032 date stands.

Mon 16 Nov: store input to Q92-034 and 3e area (3); re-read at source (Additional Articles Art. 4, three months before the term ends; election act Art. 39, ten days before): the window is 1 Nov 2031 to about 21 Jan 2032, so never say the vote is fixed in January.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; add the 2008 legislative vote (held in January 2008, apart from the March presidential vote; check it in the CEC database) so before that legislators were elected in December is not wrong by omission; presidential 2000-08 dates rest on a mirror.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; co-sponsors hear the range knowing the election date only if the meetings fall after about March 2031: the case gives no meeting month and the move stays 1 Jan 2031 (NUMBERS 8r); two cases.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; 28 Nov 2026 is scheduled, 12 days away, not a recent vote; re-read at source: Art. 33 names 25 Dec 2030 only as the day amended paras 5-6 apply to councillors taking office, so say the law implies it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3): election risk sits in central money, while a city pledge crosses no local vote; say Laura pays in late December 2032 (IBTM cash 20-22 Dec 2032, NUMBERS 8h), not about 18 Dec, which NUMBERS does not carry; city building money often rides on central grants.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; restates that the ten are owned in Treasuries; elections set when co-sponsors decide, never what the Treasuries pay; assumes unchanged laws and no dissolution.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a caveat to Q92-002 to 006 (a dissolution restarts the calendar); nothing in the plan rests on it; whether one has happened is unread.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, input to Q92-011 and 016: ministers who heard a 2031 pledge resign at least formally before 1 Feb 2032; fixed-term boards stay.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; background to Q92-011's second resignation; a courtesy, so 2032 could differ.
Mon 16 Nov: store input to Q92-016: in 2024 the cabinet was caretaker for 123 days (checked: 18 Jan to 20 May 2024), the months when 2033 estimates would start; one year read.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3) or 3d, a Taiwan fact a judge remembers; re-read at source (moc.gov.tw past ministers, page dated 7 Aug 2026): every term date exact, a new minister at each of 2016, 2020, 2024; 212 days rests on 18 Dec, not in NUMBERS: say about seven months before she pays; three cases, so on every precedent, never will.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, paired with Q92-012 (dates re-read at source: Lung to 7 Dec 2014, Lee to 30 Jan 2023); why each left is unread, so never say the local elections caused it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; NCAF's board runs on three-year terms off the election clock; quote the renewal cap's exact words before use (at most half re-appointed means at least half new).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; NCAF's board is shielded from elections but its government money goes through the same central vote; pairs with Q10d-024.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3), input to Q92-034: the 2033 central budget is the new legislature's first, drafted by a cabinet a few days old when estimates are due; the March policy ceiling (Art. 30) comes from the outgoing cabinet.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3 evidence: public 2033 money on the record passes in January 2033, after Laura pays; about 18 Dec 2032 is not in NUMBERS (say late December, cash 20-22 Dec, NUMBERS 8h); three cases and 9 of 11 late anyway (Q49-010), so the first-budget effect adds little.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; 2032 money voted by the outgoing legislature serves no part of Laura's December 2032 contribution or 2033 reserve.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3): an election delays public money, it does not erase it; re-read at source (law.moj.gov.tw, Art. 13, amended 24 Jun 2024): budget bills and petitions are the only bills carried over; pairs with Q92-020.
Mon 16 Nov: store, the other side of Q92-019: a pledge needing a new law or special act is weaker across an election; CNA's report, not the legislature's own records.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a reshuffle can pull a budget already sent (2009, re-sent in a week); a stimulus special budget, never set beside any claim that Taiwan cut arts money in a recession.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a new government moved money to local buildings within ten weeks in 2008; money added in a slowing economy, consistent with Q10d-020 (CANON B4).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the culture part of the 2008 plan reached local sites (94.04% spent); grants to cities, not private bodies; audit read in part.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3) or 3d contrast: new central money for a local building waited for each council's vote (8.48% spent by end-September 2008); Laura's money needs no vote; pairs with Q92-026.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the 2016 change also produced special building money for cities, 14 months after the inauguration; its culture lines are Q49's.
Mon 16 Nov: store, second case for Q92-024: even the forward-looking act left the council vote in place.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the 2024 revenue-sharing change moved money from the centre to cities by law; name no party; +80% is Keel arithmetic (checked 842.9 over 467.6).

Mon 16 Nov: store only; at least three times in a year is partly verified (the first two amendments' order and promulgation unread): say changed in Dec 2024 and again in 2025 until the sequence is read.

Mon 16 Nov: store, adds to Q49-015: an August grant letter is not yet money; general grants to cities cut after the FY2025 vote, a non-recession year and not arts money, so never a Taiwan cut-in-a-recession line (CANON B4).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the link between the budget office's review and the village grant dropping cities is Keel's reading of timing, no stated cause.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or Table 3 design note: watch the Ministry's notices, not the election; count changes, not the 2008 creation: 2 of 12 within a year after an inauguration against about 3.3 expected (Keel arithmetic); the 16-month rate is Q10d-007's.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the 2027 village round opened 16 Nov 2026, extending Q10d-008's windows: the 2033 round would open about Nov 2032, before the new legislature's first budget passes.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note at most a phrase (Table 3 is at its one-page limit): a watch, never a reason (IPS l.17); election expected, not fixed, in January 2032.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3), the strongest clause: public 2033 money will be voted by a legislature not yet elected when Laura states her range, while her figure is owned (NUMBERS 4, after the move); say elected after she states it (expected January 2032; the law allows 1 Nov 2031 to about 21 Jan 2032), not elected in 2032; a cabinet formed that May is 2024's practice.
Mon 16 Nov: store, or Laura's own diligence; 3d's out column excludes the residency's fundraising beyond describing her contribution; a Keel suggestion, not a funder's practice read at source.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q3b-027 (a co-sponsor falling short draws on her flexibility, never the Treasuries); adds only that an election-year delay is that case.
